what: CSX runs a freight railroad across the eastern United States, moving coal, chemicals, cars, farm goods and intermodal containers over roughly 20,000 route miles between the Atlantic coast and the Mississippi.
customers: Manufacturers, energy and chemical producers, carmakers, farm shippers and intermodal logistics firms.
money: chemicals, agricultural goods, metals, cars and forest products
containers and trailers moved between ports, terminals and inland markets
thermal and metallurgical coal for power plants and export
moat: Track that cannot be rebuilt: rights of way through the eastern US are effectively unobtainable, leaving only two railroads serving the region.
risks: Volumes have been falling as coal declines and industrial demand softens
Service problems invite shipper complaints and regulatory attention
Rail unions and safety rules raise operating costs
A proposed rail merger elsewhere in the industry could reshape competition
opportunities: Rail is far cheaper and lower-emission than trucking for long hauls
Industrial plants being built along its network create new freight
Operating margins above 30% mean recovering volumes would lift profit quickly
watch: The operating ratio and carload volumes by commodity group.
